extracted.intended_audience: inventors, startup founders, corporate IP departments, patent attorneys/agents, and patent illustrators preparing PCT (international) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing examiner‑ready drawings for PCT (Rule 11) international patent applications, including nation‑specific adaptations for national phase entry. Focuses on technical illustration, formatting, and compliance checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO PCT Rule 11 compliance (suitable for direct reproduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under WIPO PCT Rule 11, drawings must be 'suitable for direct reproduction' — every figure must be clear, durable, and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal deficiencies under Rule 11 can trigger WIPO formal notices and delay international filing dates; PCT drawings must be designed to survive review by WIPO's International Bureau and by each national office in national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred paper size A4 (210 × 297 mm); U.S. letter acceptable. Minimum margins: top 2.5 cm, left 2.5 cm, right 1.5 cm, bottom 1.0 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All sheets should be formatted to A4 with standard WIPO Rule 11 margins; page size and margins are verified on every sheet before delivery to avoid margin-related formal objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line weight and reproduction quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines must be durable, clean, and black — no faint, gray, or thin strokes that will not survive reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render lines in solid black at weights verified for clean reproduction and test drawings at standard WIPO reduction ratios to ensure clarity after reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lettering size minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: All characters and numerals must meet a minimum height of 3.2 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set all text, reference numerals, and figure labels at minimum 3.2 mm and check character size on every sheet to avoid rejections for small lettering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is permitted only if it does not reduce clarity of the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply shading in ways that maintain clarity upon reproduction; avoid shading that obscures detail or causes reproduction ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference numerals consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference numerals must correspond to the description and be consistent throughout all sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a reference numeral master list before drafting; cross-check all numerals against the specification to ensure consistency and to prevent inconsistencies between sheets and description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure must be clearly labeled (Fig. 1, Fig. 2, etc.) on every sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label every figure on every sheet and supply a complete figure description list for incorporation into the specification to prevent figure‑label related objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color usage restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required to be black and white; color is permitted only with a special request to WIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit color drawings unless a special request is made and accepted; default to black and white to avoid filing complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and discernibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be large enough that all details are discernible upon reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure figures are drawn at sizes and scales that preserve detail after reduction; verify discernibility across intended reproduction sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT drawings should contain only graphical content — no tables, flowing text, or nonstructural chemical formulas (per Rule 11.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove or relocate any text/tables/forbidden content out of the drawing sheets to the specification; keep drawing sheets strictly graphical to meet Rule 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient number of views / completeness of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a sufficient number of views to constitute a complete disclosure of the invention; the count depends on complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan a complete figure set during consultation to ensure every claimed feature is illustrated; simple inventions may need 1–3 sheets while complex inventions may require 10+ sheets. For design patents, prepare a minimum of seven standard head‑on views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of technical illustrations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate figure types for the invention: exploded views, cross‑sectional views, perspective views, elevation views, flow charts, block diagrams, circuit diagrams, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select view types to make claimed features visible and unambiguous; multi‑figure sheets must be clearly labeled and organized for examiner review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation for national phase office requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT drawings must often be adapted to meet specific national office rules (e.g., USPTO 37 CFR 1.84, EPO Rule 46 EPC, JPO, CNIPA, KIPO, CIPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare drawings to the higher PCT standard from the start to reduce later objections; adapt broken line usage, paper size, numbering, and other office‑specific conventions when entering national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: File formats and naming conventions for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Final drawings should be delivered in filing‑ready formats such as PDF (for ePCT), and/or high‑resolution TIFF or DXF, properly named and organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide files named and organized to the attorney's preferred filing conventions and compatible with ePCT/Patent Center submission workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal compliance review and quality assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Every drawing set should undergo a full internal quality and compliance review against WIPO Administrative Instructions, PCT Rule 11, and applicable national standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a checklist‑style internal review to catch margin, line weight, lettering, numbering, and content issues before delivery to prevent formal notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction policy and revision availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide revisions and corrections to drawings if formal objections arise; SNS offers unlimited revisions and will correct drawings they prepared at no charge if objected to for Rule 11 formal compliance (except where outside their control).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include guarantees and revision workflows as part of service to remediate WIPO deficiency notices and to minimize international correction costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and mitigate consequences of non‑compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Non‑compliant drawings can trigger WIPO formal deficiency notices, national phase drawing objections, prosecution ambiguity, and multiplied correction costs across jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that drawing deficiencies can delay or damage priority claims and prosecution strategy; invest in PCT‑standard drawings at filing to avoid compounded international correction costs.
